An agronomist plans to plant $x$ hectares of wheat and $y$ hectares of barley on one farm. The plan must satisfy the system below.

$x + y \le 40$
$4x - 2y < 16$
items.stem: If the point $(12, y)$ is a solution to the given system of inequalities, which of the following could be the value of $y$?
items.explanation: Substitute $x = 12$ into each inequality. The first gives $12 + y \le 40$, so $y \le 28$. The second gives $48 - 2y < 16$, so $-2y < -32$. Dividing by $-2$ flips the sign, so $y > 16$. Together the conditions are $16 < y \le 28$, and only 22 falls in that range.

A.why: You divided $-2y < -32$ by $-2$ without flipping the sign and got $y < 16$. Check it: $4(12) - 2(10) = 28$, which is not less than 16.

B.why: 16 is the boundary value of the strict inequality. $4(12) - 2(16) = 16$, and 16 is not less than 16, so this point is on the line, not in the solution region.

D.why: 30 satisfies the second inequality, but you didn't check the first: $12 + 30 = 42$, which is more than 40 hectares.

D.why: $(3, 6)$ lies exactly on the boundary line $2x - 3y = -12$. The first inequality is strict, so $-12 > -12$ is false and points on the boundary are not solutions.
